summary: Police have increased security in provinces bordering Cambodia to ensure safety for advance voting scheduled for February 2. title: Security Tightened at Border Ahead of Advance Voting

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet assured that the Cambodian government will mobilize the national budget and partner assistance to protect and restore infrastructure for internally displaced people (IDPs) affected by the border conflict. title: Cambodian PM pledges support for IDPs; ASEAN ministers discuss border de-escalation

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet emphasized that Cambodia has not ceded any land to Thailand. He stated that the government chose a peaceful path through international law and diplomatic mechanisms rather than violence to ensure a lasting solution. He rejected rumors that the ceasefire involved giving up territory, affirming that surveying and border management work continues under international law.
title: Hun Manet: Cambodia Has Not Given Up Sovereignty Claims

summary: The Ministry of Interior reported that between Jan 31 and Feb 1, 753 more displaced civilians returned to their homes. Since the Dec 27, 2025 ceasefire, about 83% of the 640,000 displaced persons have returned, but 111,509 people remain in camps. title: Ministry of Interior: 753 more displaced persons return home

title: Air Force says Thai forces on standby after repeated provocations

Cambodia stated it would not recognize any border alterations resulting from the use of force.

The government is assessing damage to schools and infrastructure for reconstruction.
title: Govt prepares salve after border displacement salvo

Thailand's Ministry of Defense denied the claims, stating they are adhering to the joint agreement to maintain existing troop deployments without further reinforcement.
title: Cambodian PM says Thailand is occupying territory after Trump-brokered ceasefire

summary: Reporting from Washington, Hun Manet urged Thailand to allow the Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) to begin demarcation immediately. He noted that technical work has been delayed, with Thailand citing its February 8, 2026, election as a reason for postponement. The Cambodian leader stressed that while ties with the US and China are strong, the border remains a critical flashpoint that requires international attention through the newly formed 'Board of Peace'.
title: Cambodia alleges Thailand violating territorial agreement

summary: The ongoing border tension between Cambodia and Thailand has caused a severe economic slump in Thailand's Aranyaprathet district. Local markets, including Rong Kluea Market, have seen many shops close due to the border remaining shut since mid-2025. Local residents express concern over financial strain and fear a third round of border clashes.
title: Border dispute causes Aranyaprathet's economy to decline sharply

summary: An extraordinary committee from the Senate visited the border areas in Sisaket province to evaluate the pros and cons of canceling the MOUs signed in 2000 and 2001. This follows growing domestic pressure and political promises to scrap the agreements amidst the ongoing maritime and land border disputes.
title: Senate Committee visits Sisaket border to study MOU 2000/2001 cancellation

summary: An investigative report claims that the conflict has resulted in approximately 149 deaths and displaced 640,000 civilians. The report criticizes Thailand for rejecting multiple mediation offers from the U.S., China, and Malaysia, and alleges the use of disproportionate force, including cluster munitions in late 2025. It also highlights the link between border tensions and the crackdown on Cambodian-based scam centers.
title: How Thailand Turned a Border Dispute Into an Illegal War

summary: The Ministry of Interior reported that while 89% of the 640,000 people displaced by the conflict have returned home, 70,516 people (mostly women and children) remain unable to return. The ministry accused Thailand of 'insincere activities' including digging canals, building roads, and filling in ponds in Banteay Meanchey province, which violates the ASEAN Charter and UN principles. They fully support the government's protest against Thai military actions in Thma Puok and Ou Chrov districts.
title: Ministry of Interior: 1,434 more displaced persons return home

summary: The Thai Situation Center issued a clarification regarding 'inaccurate' international media reports. It denied claims that Thailand's military response was disproportionate, explaining that the use of F-16 aircraft was a necessary self-defense measure under UN Charter Article 51. The center claimed Cambodian forces initiated attacks on Thai military and civilian areas first, and the Thai airstrikes strictly targeted military positions to protect citizens.
title: Thai Situation Center Rebuts Foreign Media Claims Over F-16 Usage

summary: Recent developments highlight a shift in Cambodian diplomacy, using the 'Board of Peace' meeting to spotlight the Thai military occupation. Cambodia is reportedly planning to build 3,000 houses for displaced residents near the border, while analysts warn that ongoing conflicts and regional sanctions make ambitious trade targets between the two nations unrealistic for the 2026 fiscal year.
title: Asia Daily: February 19, 2026

summary: The Japanese government has allocated $1 million to support Cambodian migrant workers who have returned from Thailand due to the ongoing border conflict. The funds aim to facilitate re-employment and social stability for those displaced or forced to leave their jobs because of the military and diplomatic tensions.
title: Japan Provides $1M for Promoting Employment of Returning Migrant Workers Affected by the Border Conflict

summary: U.S. Deputy Secretary Landau met with PM Hun Manet in Washington to discuss the Cambodia-Thailand border situation. The U.S. commended Cambodia's participation as a founding member of the Board of Peace. The discussions also covered security cooperation and efforts to combat international online scam operations targeting Americans, which has become a secondary point of friction in the border dispute.
title: Deputy Secretary Landau’s Meeting with Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet

summary: Tourism operators in seven provinces along the Thailand-Cambodia border are appealing for government stimulus. Despite the current ceasefire, domestic and international tourism has plummeted since mid-2025 due to the conflict, leaving businesses in Ubon Ratchathani, Sisaket, and Sa Kaeo struggling.
title: Thai-Cambodian border provinces seek tourism recovery measures

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet stated that Thai forces remain inside Cambodian territory beyond the boundary lines claimed by Bangkok, causing significant hardship for local communities. Speaking from the United States while attending a 'Board of Peace' meeting, he called for the Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) to urgently resume technical work. He noted that despite the Dec 27 ceasefire, Thai troops have placed shipping containers and barbed wire across roads, preventing villagers from accessing their lands.
title: Hun Manet urges swift border demarcation as Thai Troops remain in Cambodian territory

summary: The Thai Navy arrested 5 Chinese nationals and 1 Cambodian fleeing into Chanthaburi from Cambodia. They were found with 270 mobile phones and numerous SIM cards. The Navy spokesperson criticized Cambodia, stating the escape reflects a 'structural failure' of the neighboring state to prevent its territory from being used as a base for international cybercrime (Cyber Scams).
title: Thai Navy Arrests Cyber Scam Gang Fleeing Cambodia with 270 Phones

summary: Thai officials have formally rejected claims by Cambodian PM Hun Manet that Thailand is occupying territory beyond agreed zones. Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow is preparing to clarify facts regarding the border situation and the regional scammer crisis at the UN Human Rights Council in Geneva later this month. Military communication channels remain active despite the verbal sparring.
title: Thailand Rebuts Hun Manet’s Border Claims

summary: Tensions remain high as the Thai Army Region 2 monitors movement of nearly 10,000 Cambodian troops near Chong Bok. Diplomatically, Thailand is using the issue of Cambodia-based online scam centers to counter Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet's international lobbying regarding border disputes. Meanwhile, the Thai Foreign Ministry is gathering historical documents from France to prepare for technical border talks.
title: Thai-Cambodia Border Diplomacy: 'Online Scams' Pressure Hun Manet

summary: The 2nd Army Region reported 8 wildfire surveillance points along the border. While smoke and fires were observed on the Cambodian side near the Thai border, the situation is currently under control. Military units are monitoring the situation closely to prevent the fire from spreading into Thai territory, particularly in Ubon Ratchathani and Surin.
title: 2nd Army Region Monitors 8 Wildfire Spots Along Thai-Cambodia Border

source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan
summary: Japan's Ambassador for Mekong Cooperation, Hayashi Teiji, is scheduled to visit Thailand, Cambodia, and the Philippines (ASEAN Chair) from February 23 to 27. The mission aims to encourage the steady implementation of the December 27 ceasefire. Japan has already provided equipment to the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) and is engaging in diplomatic efforts to ensure regional stability amid the fragile border situation.
title: Visit of Ambassador for Mekong Cooperation HAYASHI to Thailand, Cambodia, and the Philippines

summary: The Royal Thai Army has responded to allegations from Cambodian PM Hun Manet, insisting that the disputed areas belong to Thailand. Military officials criticized the lack of discipline among Cambodian troops newly deployed to the area and stated that Thai forces are prepared and disciplined in their defense of the frontier. The Army is coordinating with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to officially counter Cambodia's narrative.
title: Thai Army Slams Cambodia, Reaffirms Territory as Thai

summary: Thai media reports that Cambodian soldiers allegedly started forest fires along the border to harass Thai troops. However, strong winds blew the flames back into Cambodia, destroying a wood processing factory belonging to a deputy district chief and over 60 civilian homes in Battambang and Preah Vihear provinces. Thai forces remain on high alert due to the smoke and proximity of the fires to Thai military bases.
title: Cambodian Soldiers' Border Fire Backfires, Burns Own Villages

summary: The Royal Thai Navy's First Fleet intercepted an unregistered Cambodian wooden boat in the eastern sea border. The vessel was found smuggling a large quantity of seafood to be transferred to Thai fishing boats to avoid customs. Three Cambodian crew members were arrested and sent to Khlong Yai Police Station for legal action.
title: Navy Seizes Cambodian Vessel Smuggling Seafood to Thai Boats

summary: Thai media reports on Cambodian PM Hun Manet's interview with Fox News Digital, where he alleged Thai military advancement into overlapping claim areas has displaced over 80,000 Cambodians. The Thai military has not yet issued a formal counter-statement to these specific international allegations, though the tone in Thai media remains skeptical of the '80,000' figure.
title: Hun Manet complains to Fox News about Thai 'encroachment' affecting 80,000 displaced people

summary: Speaking to international media in the US, PM Hun Manet detailed how Thai forces have occupied areas beyond the agreed border lines using 'unilateral maps.' This occupation includes the installation of trenches and barriers that block access to villages. Consequently, around 80,000 Cambodians remain unable to return to their lands in Banteay Meanchey and other border provinces, prolonging a humanitarian crisis that began during the 2025 fighting.
title: Border map dispute nixes displaced people's return

summary: Government spokesperson Pen Bona stated that the border tension has reached the highest level of global discourse after US President Donald Trump referenced the 'nasty war' between the two nations during his speech on Feb 19. Cambodia alleges that Thai occupation and restrictions are preventing over 70,000 displaced Cambodians from returning to their homes.
title: Cambodia-Thailand border spat gains global attention at Board of Peace meeting

summary: Spokesperson Pen Bona expressed hope that PM Hun Manet's diplomatic mission in Washington will help restore stability. The government maintains that Thai troops are currently occupying several areas inside Cambodia’s sovereign borders. Analysts suggest that engaging global media like Reuters and Fox News is a strategic move to expose Thailand's perceived 'aggression'.
title: Cambodia says border dispute with Thailand will be restored after Hun Manet's presence at Peace Council meeting

summary: The Thailand-Cambodia Border Defense Command reported 7 heat hotspots/forest fires near the border in Surin and Sisaket provinces. Most fires are on the Cambodian side, some only 500 meters from the Thai border. While the cause is attributed to agricultural burning and foraging, the proximity adds logistical difficulty to the current military standby status in areas like Preah Vihear and Don Tual.
title: Border Forces report 7 major forest fires near Thai-Cambodian border

summary: In Washington D.C., PM Hun Manet met with Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan. The meeting touched upon the roots of the Cambodia-Thailand border conflict. Hun Manet briefed the Turkish diplomat on recent developments and reaffirmed Cambodia's stance on resolving the dispute peacefully based on international law. The Turkish Foreign Minister expressed interest in the issue and hoped for long-term peace between the two neighbors.
title: Turkish Foreign Minister hopes Cambodia-Thailand can achieve permanent peace in the future

summary: During a meeting in Washington, US Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau thanked PM Hun Manet for Cambodia's founding role in the Board of Peace. Landau stated that President Trump is proud to contribute to stopping the fighting and that the US will work to ensure a lasting peace. Hun Manet briefed the US on the latest ground situation and reaffirmed Cambodia's peaceful position based on international law.
title: US Deputy Secretary of State Reaffirms Support for Lasting Peace along Cambodia–Thailand Border

summary: During a meeting with CPP officials in Svay Rieng, Samdech Men Sam An briefed members on the border developments. She stated that the government is working hard to prevent the border situation with Thailand from escalating into a more serious conflict. The meeting aimed to update local officials on the political situation so they can manage public sentiment and maintain peace and stability at the grassroots level.
title: Cambodian leaders strive to manage situation, avoid serious problems

summary: The Royal Thai Armed Forces have officially released a white paper containing maps and historical evidence to justify Thai troop positions. This moves the conflict into a legal and diplomatic documentation phase, aiming to rebut PM Hun Manet's claims of 'nasty war' and territorial theft presented during his recent visit to the U.S.
title: Thai Armed Forces release 'White Paper' to counter Cambodian border claims

summary: Army Region 2 spokesperson addressed reports from Cambodian media (TFA/Khmer) claiming Thai troops opened fire at Chong An Ma, injuring a Cambodian soldier. Thailand insists no weapons were used; instead, Thai troops only gave verbal warnings to Cambodian forces moving too close to Thai lines. A Cambodian soldier was reportedly injured by 5-7 shots from an unknown source within Cambodia, and Thailand urges both sides to stick to the GBC ceasefire guidelines.
title: Army Region 2 denies shooting Cambodian soldiers at Chong An Ma, labels it 'Fake News'

summary: Atlantic Council CEO Frederick Kempe met PM Hun Manet in Washington to discuss the roots of the border dispute. Hun Manet emphasized that Thai forces are currently occupying locations deep inside Cambodian territory, which he claimed is a factual reality on the ground, not an unfounded accusation. He requested the Council to help share the truth of the conflict with the global community.
title: Atlantic Council CEO wants to learn more about Cambodia-Thailand border conflict

summary: A report citing a 'New York Editorial' claims Thailand's actions violate international law. It alleges Thai forces used cluster bombs and air strikes deep in Cambodian territory, causing 149 deaths and displacing 640,000 civilians. The report characterizes Thailand's 'online scam' accusations as a pretext for invasion and illegal blockades of fuel and sea routes.
title: American media 'unmasks Thailand', showing the world the transformation of border dispute into illegal war

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a formal protest against the 'unauthorized presence' of Royal Thai Navy vessels in Cambodian territorial waters on February 22. The government described the move as an unlawful exercise of law enforcement and a violation of sovereignty. This follows reports of a fishing vessel with Cambodian crew being apprehended by Thai authorities recently.
title: The Royal Government of Cambodia formally protests the unauthorized presence of Royal Thai Navy vessels

summary: Cambodia has filed a formal protest against the Royal Thai Navy for alleged unauthorized presence in its territorial waters off Koh Kong. The incident involved the arrest of three Cambodians and the seizure of their fishing vessel approximately 7.2 nautical miles from Koh Yor. Cambodia labels this a 'clear violation' of international law and sovereignty.
title: Thai Navy Breached Cambodia's Sovereign Waters, Conducted Unauthorised Patrols

summary: Royal Government Spokesperson Pen Bona formally accused Thai military forces of a territorial incursion, alleging they remain positioned deep inside Cambodian territory. The spokesperson claimed Thai troops are using barbed wire and shipping containers to block nearly 80,000 displaced Cambodian civilians from returning home. Phnom Penh reiterated its rejection of military force to alter borders and urged Thailand to allow the Joint Border Commission to resume work following the conclusion of Thailand's elections.
title: Cambodia accuses Thailand of incursion, calls for de-escalation amid diplomatic push

summary: Reports suggest a possible 'setup' by Cambodian forces after they claimed a soldier was wounded by Thai fire at Chong An Ma. Thai security sources argue the wound appears inconsistent with a bullet strike, possibly being a scratch or cut instead. The report emphasizes adhering to the ceasefire and GBC agreements despite these accusations.
title: Cambodia Staging Incident? Experts Spot Irregularities in Soldier's Wounds After Shooting Claim

summary: Two Cambodian journalists, Phorn Sopheap and Pheap Pheara, are appealing their 14-year prison sentences for treason. They were convicted in December 2025 for posting Facebook photos of border clashes with Thailand, which allegedly included images of land mines. International rights groups have condemned the sentences as a suppression of press freedom.
title: 2 Cambodian journalists appeal treason convictions over a photo from Thai border clash

summary: Thai security agencies responded to Cambodian claims that a soldier was shot from the Thai side at Chong An Ma on February 20. Experts noted that photographs of the soldier's knee injury do not align with forensic patterns of gunshot wounds in terms of shape, size, or surrounding tissue. Authorities urged both sides to follow the GBC (General Border Committee) framework to maintain stability.
title: Cambodian Soldier Claims Shot at 'Chong An Ma'; Thai Security Says Wounds Don't Match Gunfire

summary: The Second Army Region reported that wildfires are still active at three locations near Khao Satta Som and Don Tual Castle, originating from the Cambodian side. The fires are suspected to be caused by agricultural burning or hunting. Thai security forces are patrolling and creating firebreaks to prevent the fire from crossing the border, while the situation at Khao Phra Viharn (Pha Mo I Daeng) remains normal.
title: Wildfires continue at 3 spots along Thai-Cambodian border in Si Sa Ket

summary: Following Cambodian accusations of encroachment, the Royal Thai Navy released a detailed timeline and GPS coordinates (Lat 11° 32.63' N, Long 102° 50.54' E) of the detention of a Cambodian boat. The Navy insists the boat was 2 nautical miles inside Thai waters near Trat. Three Cambodian crew members were detained for illegal fishing.
title: Navy confirms Cambodian fishing boat seized in Thai waters

summary: Maj Gen Winthai Suvaree, Army spokesperson, addressed allegations from a foreign page ('The New York Editorial') claiming Thailand used disproportionate force. He clarified that F-16s were used only against military targets after Cambodia fired heavy weapons first. He denied the use of cluster munitions against people, stating that DPICM was used on equipment, and claimed the death of a Cambodian child was due to old explosives, not Thai actions.
title: Army rebuts seven fake news claims on Thai-Cambodia border

summary: The Royal Thai Army has rejected an international report claiming Thailand used excessive force, including F-16 airstrikes, to influence domestic elections in Bangkok. Army spokesperson Maj Gen Winthai Suvaree stated that operations are strictly 'legitimate self-defence' under the UN Charter and denied using the border dispute for political gain.
title: Thai army insists Cambodia border actions not politically motivated

summary: During his visit to Washington D.C., PM Hun Manet informed leaders from the UN, Hungary, Indonesia, and Vietnam about the 'real situation' where Thai forces have allegedly invaded and occupied Cambodian territory. He called for the full implementation of existing agreements and the safe return of civilians to their homes, stressing that peace remains Cambodia's core value.
title: Ministry of Foreign Affairs: PM Hun Manet informs counterparts about real situation on border

summary: During the Inaugural Meeting of the Board of Peace in Washington, D.C., PM Hun Manet briefed international counterparts and media on the border conflict. He called for the full implementation of existing agreements, a peaceful settlement according to international law, and the safe return of Cambodian civilians to their homes.
title: PM Hun Manet Briefs All Counterparts on Cambodia-Thailand Border Situation, Reaffirms Peace as Core Value

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet attended the inaugural Board of Peace meeting in Washington, DC, where he described the current ceasefire with Thailand as 'fragile.' He highlighted the ongoing tensions to world leaders, seeking international attention to the border dispute that saw major clashes in late 2025. He emphasized Cambodia's commitment to peace but noted that the situation remains unstable despite the US-brokered agreement.
title: Hun Manet calls attention to ‘fragile’ ceasefire at meeting of world leaders in US

summary: Government spokesperson Pen Bona stated that Cambodia remains committed to the ceasefire agreement reached in late 2025 despite the ongoing territorial disputes and presence of Thai troops in disputed zones. He emphasized that the Cambodian leadership's priority is maintaining peace and adhering to international law.
title: Pen Bona: In the spirit of loving peace, Cambodia continues to respect the ceasefire

summary: While Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow accused Cambodia of provoking tensions, Cambodian media highlights shipping containers set up by Thai soldiers in Chouk Chey village, Banteay Meanchey. The Cambodian government is using international platforms to report what it describes as Thai infringements on sovereignty, countering Thai claims that the issue should only be handled bilaterally without third-party involvement.
title: Cambodia tells its side of the story on world stage

summary: The Thai Ministry of Defense has proposed a gradual withdrawal of troops from the 798km border with Cambodia to the Defense Council to manage costs. Minister Nattaphon noted that while military presence is still needed in areas recaptured in December, such as Chong An Ma and Phu Makua, the ministry plans to upgrade border fencing with electronic monitoring. Some clash zones may be developed into tourist attractions in the future.
title: Thailand proposes troop cutback along Cambodian border to reduce costs

summary: Lieutenant General Maly Socheata categorically denied Thai military reports that Cambodian forces fired a 40mm grenade at a Thai patrol near Preah Vihear on Feb 24. She stated that Cambodian forces heard explosions on the Thai side but did not fire any weapons, urging Thailand to stop spreading 'fake news' that increases border tensions.
title: Press Release of Lt. Gen. Maly Socheata, Spokesperson for the Ministry of National Defence

summary: Cambodian Ambassador to France, Luy David, addressed the International Organization of La Francophonie (OIF), stating that 60,000 displaced Cambodians, including many women and girls, are unable to return home due to Thai military infrastructure like shipping containers and barbed wire on 'sovereign Cambodian land.' The report emphasizes the humanitarian impact of the ongoing border tension.
title: Ambassador to France Briefs OIF on Vulnerability of Cambodian Women Amid Thai Invasion

summary: An analysis of Thailand's observer status at Donald Trump's inaugural 'Board of Peace' (BOP) meeting in Washington. While Cambodia is a founding member, Thai media were concerned about the Thai flag appearing in the background. The incoming Thai government is weighing the implications of joining the BOP, especially given Hun Manet's active praise of Trump and his nomination of Trump for the Nobel Peace Prize, which could complicate existing border tensions.
title: The fuss about Thailand and the BOP

summary: Thai Defense Minister Gen. Nattaphon Nakpanich (Big Lek) has publicly criticized Cambodian troops for lacking discipline and intentionally starting forest fires along the border to harass Thai authorities. He warned Cambodia to stop spreading 'fake news' regarding allegations that Thai soldiers shot Cambodian personnel. He also supported the construction of permanent electronic fences, particularly in the Khlong Luek and Thmor Da areas, to prevent further provocations.
title: 'Big Lek' Blasts Cambodia: Slams Undisciplined Soldiers for Setting Forest Fires to Harass Thai Border

summary: Thai military units reported an exchange of fire with Cambodian forces in the Phan Hin Paed Kon area of Sisaket province. The incident reportedly began when Cambodian troops fired a 40mm grenade (M79) at a Thai patrol, prompting Thai soldiers to return fire. No Thai casualties were reported, and the situation has since calmed, though troops remain on high alert. The Thai military suggests the incident may have been caused by a lack of coordination during a Cambodian troop rotation.
title: Border Tensions! Thai and Cambodian Troops Clash at Phan Hin Paed Kon

summary: Civil society organizations released a statement noting that 170,000 civilians remain displaced and unable to return home due to military presence and infrastructure damage. The report highlights incursions in Cambodian territory and the destruction of civilian assets, urging both nations to honor the ASEAN Charter and previous ceasefire commitments.
title: Statement Calling for Legal and Peaceful Resolution of the Cambodia–Thailand Border Conflict

summary: Ambassador Luy David reported to the Francophonie Governance Council that over 60,000 Cambodians, including many women and children, cannot return home because Thai troops have placed shipping containers and barbed wire in occupied areas. He stated that 32 people died and 95 were injured during the 21-day 'invasion war' in December 2025. Currently, 35,099 women remain in temporary safety camps as of February 23, 2026, due to Thai military obstructions and unexploded ordnance.
title: Cambodian Ambassador highlights pain of Cambodian women due to Thai invasion at Governance Council meeting

summary: Foreign Affairs Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow stated that Cambodia's leadership continues to use 'old tactics' of fabricating news to pressure Thailand on the global stage. He revealed that he recently met with UNESCO's Director-General to clarify that Thailand did not intend to damage the Preah Vihear Temple, blaming the damage on Cambodia using the site as a military base and weapons cache. Thailand maintains a stance of restraint while seeking to rebuild mutual trust.
title: Sihasak Claims Cambodian Leader Still Fabricating Stories to Discredit Thailand Internationally

summary: Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow rejected claims by Cambodian PM Hun Manet that Thai forces are occupying Cambodian territory. Sihasak stated that both nations agreed to a ceasefire where troops stay in current positions, though he described the peace as 'fragile.' He accused Cambodia of 'internationalising' the conflict to stir sentiment.
title: Thai FM hits back at Cambodia's 'occupation' claim in France 24 interview

summary: The Ministry of National Defence officially rejected Thai media reports claiming Cambodian forces fired a 40mm grenade at a Thai patrol in Preah Vihear on Feb 24. Spokesperson Maly Socheata stated that RCAF troops heard explosions from the Thai side first and contacted Thai counterparts to clarify that no Cambodian weapons were fired.
title: Cambodia denies Thai claims of grenade launcher fire near Preah Vihear border

summary: Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow delivered a statement at the UN Human Rights Council in Geneva, rejecting Cambodia's accusations of territorial encroachment. He described Cambodia's narrative as distorted and 'demonizing' Thailand. Sihasak emphasized that Thailand remains committed to the December ceasefire and peaceful diplomacy but blamed the recent friction on Cambodian provocations and interference in Thai internal politics.
title: FM Counters Cambodia’s Border Remarks, Reaffirms Thailand’s Stance

summary: The Thai army reported an exchange of fire with Cambodian forces in Sisaket province on Tuesday morning. According to the Thai statement, Cambodian forces fired a 40mm grenade at a Thai patrol, prompting a return shot from an M79 launcher as a warning. No injuries were reported. The Thai military suggested the incident might have been caused by a rotation of new Cambodian troops unfamiliar with the area.
title: Thai army says exchanged fire with Cambodia at border

summary: The Ministry of Digital Economy and Society (DE) issued a warning about viral fake news claiming Cambodia has deployed PHL-03 long-range rocket launchers near the border, targeting Nakhon Ratchasima. The ministry clarified that this is false information intended to cause public panic during the ongoing border tensions and urged citizens to follow only official government updates.
title: DE Warns of Fake News Regarding Cambodian Missile Deployment

summary: Cambodia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs lodged a formal protest after the Royal Thai Navy arrested three Cambodian fishermen and seized their boat 7.2 nautical miles from Koh Yor Island in Koh Kong province. Officials called the act a 'clear violation of sovereignty.' While land borders are quiet, maritime tensions remain high following the 2025 conflict.
title: Cambodia protests Thai navy presence in its waters

summary: On the morning of February 24, 2026, a 40mm grenade was fired from the Cambodian side at a Thai patrol in Si Sa Ket's Kantharalak district. Thai forces responded with an M79 warning shot. The Thai military believes the incident was caused by newly rotated Cambodian troops unfamiliar with the area. No injuries were reported, and the Army Chief has ruled out further escalation.
title: Thailand blames Cambodia after brief border exchange

summary: Cambodia's Information Minister Neth Pheaktra dismissed Thai military claims that Cambodian soldiers fired a 40mm grenade near a Thai patrol in Sisaket province. Thailand's army reported returning fire as a warning, suggesting the incident might have been caused by new, inexperienced Cambodian troops during a rotation. Cambodia labeled the claims as 'fabricated' and intended to mislead public opinion.
title: Cambodia rejects claim its forces fired on Thai patrol

summary: Tensions remain high following a reported skirmish in the Sisaket province. While the Thai military accused Cambodia of violating the December ceasefire by firing a grenade, Phnom Penh officials have denied the use of any weapons. This flare-up is the first significant incident since the December 2025 truce, following a year of conflict that displaced over a million people.
title: Thailand, Cambodia dispute exchange of fire at border

summary: Maly Socheata, spokesperson for the Ministry of National Defence, strongly denied claims by the Thai military that Cambodian soldiers fired a 40mm grenade near a Thai patrol on February 24. She called the reports 'false and fabricated,' aimed at misleading the public. Military Region 4 confirmed that while explosions were heard on the Thai side, Cambodian forces were not involved.
title: Cambodia Rejects Thai Accusations of 40mm Grenade Fire

summary: The Second Army Region reported that on February 24, Cambodian forces fired a 40mm grenade at a Thai patrol near Phlan Hin Paed Kon in Si Sa Ket province. The grenade landed near the cliff edge about 2km from the base. Thai forces returned fire according to engagement rules. No Thai casualties or damage were reported, and the situation is currently under control.
title: Second Army Region confirms Thailand safe after Cambodia opened fire; Thai forces returned warning shots

summary: Thailand's military reported an exchange of fire with Cambodian forces in Sisaket province on Tuesday morning. The Thai army claims Cambodian troops fired a 40mm grenade, prompting a warning shot in return. Cambodia's Ministry of Information denied the claims, calling them 'fabricated'. The incident threatens the December truce that ended months of heavy fighting which displaced over a million people in 2025.
title: Thailand says troops exchanged fire at border, Cambodia denies ceasefire breach

summary: Cambodian Deputy PM and Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn alleged on the international stage that Thailand has established military bases within Cambodian territory. He claimed this aggression has forced over 650,000 Cambodian civilians to evacuate. This statement was met with a swift counter-rebuttal from the Thai Foreign Ministry later that day.
title: Cambodia Accuses Thailand of Building Bases on Its Territory, 650,000 Displaced

summary: Following a massive explosion at a Thai Border Patrol Police ammunition depot in Surin province on Tuesday night, Thai PM Anutin Charnvirakul clarified the incident was a technical accident caused by heat, not an attack or related to border tensions. The fire destroyed small arms ammunition, mortars, and grenades, leading to the evacuation of 300 residents. Cambodian media reported this to allay local fears of renewed border fighting.
title: Anutin clarifies that the Surin ammo warehouse fire is not related to the Cambodia-Thailand border issue

summary: A coalition of 424 Cambodian civil society organizations issued a joint statement condemning Thai military movements. They allege that Thai troops destroyed civilian homes, schools, and health centers in contested areas. The groups claim Thai airstrikes and rockets previously reached 36km inside Cambodia, and they are now calling for international accountability for the displacement of civilians.
title: Thailand accused of breaching UN, ASEAN commitments

summary: Cambodian authorities led foreign diplomats and UN agencies to Banteay Meanchey to show evidence of Thai troops allegedly occupying 760 hectares of land following a December ceasefire. Officials claim Thai forces used shipping containers and barbed wire to create a 'fait accompli' situation. The Ministry of National Defence also rejected Thai military reports of a Cambodian grenade attack in Preah Vihear.
title: Cambodia doubles down on bid to spotlight Thai occupation

summary: A major fire and multiple explosions occurred at a Thai Border Patrol Police ammunition depot in Surin province, roughly 50km from the border. The facility housed RPGs, mortar rounds, and rifle ammunition. While authorities suspect heat buildup as the cause, sabotage has not been ruled out. One officer was injured, and nearby housing was evacuated. Officials stressed there was no immediate cross-border risk.
title: Massive blast hits Thailand’s Border Patrol Police ammo depot in Surin

summary: Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow rejected claims made by Cambodia's Prak Sokhonn at the UN Human Rights Council in Geneva. Cambodia accused Thailand of occupying territory and displacing 650,000 people. Sihasak countered that the 2025 ceasefire is being undermined by Cambodia's "premeditated provocations" and landmines, while Thailand remains committed to defending its sovereignty.
title: Thai foreign minister rebuts Cambodian claims

summary: The 'Rak Chart' Party has submitted a petition to UNESCO to investigate Cambodia's registration of traditional wedding ceremonies. The party expresses concern that the attire used in the Cambodian submission is too similar to Thai national dress (Chut Thai), fearing a cultural 'claim' that could mislead the international community. They demand a transparent historical verification of shared or overlapping cultures.
title: Thai Party Urges UNESCO to Block Cambodian Wedding Tradition Claim Over 'Thai Style' Attire

summary: An ASEAN observation mission conducted between Feb 22-24 reported no major combat but confirmed limited troop movements and 2 km of new Thai barbed wire near Preah Vihear. The report notes that 150 hectares of Cambodian farmland remain inaccessible. Border trade has dropped significantly, with monthly losses estimated at $5 million due to semi-closed checkpoints at Doung, O'Smach, and Choam Sangke.
title: Cambodia-Thailand Border Tensions: From Ceasefire to Standoff

summary: Deputy Prime Minister Prak Sokhonn told the UN Human Rights Council in Geneva that Thai military operations since mid-2025 have led to 'forcible expulsions' and serious rights violations. He claimed Thai forces have built infrastructure deep inside Cambodian land, preventing 65,000 displaced people from returning home despite the current fragile ceasefire.
title: Regional stability at risk as border crisis deepens

summary: The Cambodian government is demanding Thailand send border specialists to agree on demarcation in Pursat, Oddar Meanchey, and Banteay Meanchey. The report claims Thailand occupied these areas during a '21-day invasion war' a few months ago. Civil society groups are calling for international pressure to force Thai troops to withdraw from Cambodian sovereign territory.
title: Cambodia continues to push for border demarcation as agreed while Thailand unilaterally expands new border

summary: Army Chief Gen Pana Claewplodtook stated that the recent 40mm grenade fired by Cambodian forces into Si Sa Ket originated from a point 100 meters inside Cambodian territory. The Army attributed the incident to a lack of discipline among Cambodian troops. Thailand plans to document the aggression and raise the issue at the UN Human Rights Council while maintaining a restrained military posture to avoid escalation.
title: Thai Army responds cautiously to Cambodia's grenade attack; UN human rights intervention planned

summary: The Thai government clarified against reports claiming Thailand used excessive force and cluster munitions. The PRD stated that the use of F-16s was a necessary defensive measure after Cambodian forces used heavy weapons against Thai civilian areas. They denied the use of banned cluster bombs, stating only standard DPICM rounds were used against military targets.
title: Fact Check: Response to distorted news reports (Feb 25, 2026)

summary: Maj Gen Winthai Suvaree, the army spokesman, dismissed Cambodia's claim that 650,000 civilians were displaced by Thai military operations. He described the group in question as "trespassers" on Thai sovereignty rather than displaced persons and urged Cambodia to handle its own citizens instead of distorting facts to gain international sympathy.
title: Thai Army rebuts Prak Sokhonn over ‘650,000 displaced’ claim

summary: Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow delivered a speech at the 61st UN Human Rights Council session in Geneva, responding to accusations from Cambodia. He stated that the conflict stems from repeated Cambodian provocations and interference in Thai internal politics. He described the situation as a 'tragedy' between neighbors, emphasizing that Thailand has historically provided humanitarian aid to Cambodia and has no desire for confrontation, despite current tensions and civilian casualties.
title: Thai FM Blasts Cambodia at UN, Calls Border Conflict a 'Tragedy of Relations'

summary: Army Region 2 summarized the situation regarding forest fires along the Thai-Cambodian border. While two hotspots were detected on the Cambodian side near Khao Satta Som (about 900m to 1.2km from the line), the Thai side remains normal. The fires are attributed to agricultural clearing and foraging, with Thai officials monitoring closely to prevent transboundary smoke.
title: Summary of border fires: Army Region 2 confirms Thai side is normal

summary: Local observers and opposition members in Cambodia have expressed support for the government's strong stance at the UN. The report highlights that Thai troops have allegedly occupied several villages, expelled residents by force, and replaced homes with military infrastructure like barbed wire and shipping containers. This is framed as the first time Cambodia has 'lost patience' and openly labeled Thailand an invader on the international stage despite reported Thai threats.
title: Opposition officials and observers applaud the naked exposure of Thai invaders at the UN forum

summary: In an interview in Brussels, Prime Minister Hun Manet emphasized that Cambodia seeks de-escalation and peaceful coexistence with Thailand. He denied Thai accusations that Cambodian forces fired a grenade at a patrol on February 24. He also expressed concern over the 'fragile' nature of the border situation and claimed Thai forces have ventured beyond the frontier into areas Cambodia considers its sovereign territory.
title: Cambodia wants ‘de-escalation’ in conflict with Thailand, PM tells AFP

summary: In an interview with AFP in Brussels, PM Hun Manet stated that Cambodia is seeking de-escalation and peaceful coexistence. However, he emphasized that Thai forces have moved 'far beyond' even the border lines claimed by Bangkok. He expressed readiness to accept results from a joint border commission using historical French maps to resolve the issue once and for all.
title: Samdech Thipadei tells AFP: Cambodia wants to solve dispute with Thailand peacefully

summary: The Ministry of National Defence spokeswoman, Lt. Gen. Maly Socheata, denied Thai claims that Cambodian troops fired a 40mm grenade near a Thai patrol in Sisaket on Tuesday. Cambodian military officials stated that while explosions were heard from the Thai side, no Cambodian weapons were discharged. Analysts suggest the ceasefire remains fragile due to Thailand's continued military presence in disputed areas.
title: Ceasefire tested as Cambodia denies Thai border fire claims

summary: The ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) visited the Preah Vihear Temple area on February 26 to assess damage and verify the ceasefire status. Lieutenant General Maly Socheata stated that the temple sustained heavy damage due to 'Thai military aggression.' Cambodia claims it is strictly following the October 2025 peace agreement and expects Thailand to show the same 'good faith.'
title: ASEAN Observer Team Visits Preah Vihear to Verify Post-Ceasefire Situation

summary: In an interview with AFP, PM Hun Manet stated that Cambodia is seeking a peaceful resolution and does not intend to escalate conflict. However, he accused Thailand of illegal occupation and 'fait accompli' tactics by placing containers and barbed wire in Cambodian territory following the Dec 27 ceasefire. He emphasized that Cambodia remains committed to diplomatic mechanisms despite these perceived provocations.
title: PM Hun Manet tells AFP: Cambodia does not want to increase tension, wants peaceful coexistence with Thailand

summary: In a rare international interview from Brussels, Prime Minister Hun Manet stated that Cambodia seeks de-escalation and peaceful coexistence. He described the current border situation as 'not stable' and 'fragile,' noting that while Cambodia is ready to accept historical map surveys from France, Thai forces have allegedly ventured beyond established frontiers.
title: Cambodia wants 'deescalation' in conflict with Thailand: PM

summary: A new Migrant Worker Resource Centre (MRC) has opened in Siem Reap to assist returnees affected by the ongoing border conflict. The ILO reports that the center is timely due to the mass return of Cambodian workers from Thailand amid the instability, providing legal aid and reintegration services.
title: Cambodian migrant workers receive expanded support in Siem Reap province

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Labour reported that remittances from overseas workers dropped from $2.95 billion in 2024 to $1.86 billion in 2025. This sharp decline is attributed to approximately 940,000 Cambodian workers fleeing Thailand due to the ongoing border hostilities. The conflict has forced a massive labor migration back to Cambodia, severely impacting the economy of Cambodian families reliant on Thai wages.
title: Cambodian Remittances Plummet in 2025 as Border Conflict Drives 940,000 Workers Out of Thailand

summary: Cambodia’s Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn addressed the UN Human Rights Council in Geneva, accusing the Thai military of occupying Cambodian territory and committing human rights violations. He claimed that since mid-2025, Thai operations have led to the destruction of civilian homes and the displacement of nearly 650,000 people, with over 80,000 still unable to return. Thailand's representative countered by framing the conflict as a matter of troop positioning agreed upon during the ceasefire.
title: Cambodia-Thailand border tensions spill onto the global stage at United Nations Human Rights Council

summary: The Second Army Region reported a hotspot in the Cambodian side, about 600 meters from the Thai border in Si Sa Ket province. Military patrols have been intensified to prevent the fire from crossing into Thailand. Other border areas, including Preah Vihear (Phra Wiharn) and Surin, remain normal with no combat reported in the last 24 hours.
title: Second Army Region monitors border fire 600m from line

summary: A news report shows Cambodian soldiers allegedly positioned close to Thai border plantations, observing Thai authorities. The report highlights local concerns after sounds of gunfire were heard, prompting Thai military units to move in and monitor the situation closely to protect villagers.
title: Cambodian soldiers lurking near border, gunfire heard

summary: Recent incidents, including the seizure of a Cambodian fishing boat and the alleged grenade fire in Sisaket, are straining the fragile peace. Cambodian officials state that liaison teams from both sides confirmed no weapons were fired by Khmer forces. The report notes that Thailand continues to occupy disputed territories with shipping containers and barbed wire, while Prime Minister Hun Manet seeks international arbitration through ASEAN and the UN.
title: Cambodia Rejects Thai Claims It Launched a Grenade at Thai Troops

summary: A Thai soldier patrolling the border in Surin province was seriously injured and airlifted for emergency treatment after stepping on a long-buried landmine. This incident occurred amidst the ongoing 'Thailand-Cambodia Standoff' and highlights the continued danger for personnel operating in contested border zones.
title: Thai soldier airlifted after stepping on landmine in Surin

summary: Human Rights Watch has condemned the 14-year prison sentences given to Cambodian journalists Phorn Sopheap and Pheap Pheara, who were charged with treason for reporting on the border conflict. The report also highlights the arrests of Meas Sara and Luot Sophal on incitement charges as part of a broader crackdown on freedom of speech since the conflict began.
title: Cambodian Journalists Unjustly Sentenced to 14 Years

summary: Following the 2025 border conflict, nearly 1 million Cambodian workers fled Thailand. While 630,000 have found local work, experts warn that the government must shift focus from short-term job placement to long-term economic stability and higher productivity for these returnees.
title: Cambodia Urged to Boost Job Quality and Governance to Reintegrate Returnees From Thailand

summary: The Cambodian Mine Action Authority has challenged Thai reports claiming new landmines were found along the border. Cambodian officials suggest these claims may be a tactic by Thailand to delay joint border survey work and avoid removing military positions from disputed zones near Preah Vihear.
title: Cambodian Mine Action Center calls on Thailand to show specific evidence of landmine explosions

summary: Foreign Affairs Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow, during visits to Paris and Geneva, firmly rejected allegations from Phnom Penh that Thai forces violated Cambodian territory. He reaffirmed Thailand's strict adherence to the December ceasefire and urged Cambodia to use existing bilateral channels rather than international pressure to resolve disputes.
title: Sihasak defends border conduct in Europe: ministry

summary: Prime Minister Srettha Thavisin met with the Army Chief of Staff to discuss border security, stating there is nothing to worry about. Meanwhile, the Royal Thai Navy presented evidence of newly planted landmines in Thai territory (Trat province) to ASEAN observers (AOT), accusing Cambodia of violating sovereignty and obstructing demining efforts.
title: PM meets Army Chief on border issues; Navy presents evidence against Cambodia

summary: A Thai soldier was critically injured and lost his right leg after stepping on a landmine near the border in Surin province at dawn on Friday. The Thai military stated that a preliminary check suggests the mine was an older one buried deep in the ground, rather than a newly laid device. This incident occurs during a fragile ceasefire following heavy fighting in 2025 that displaced over a million people.
title: Thai soldier loses leg in landmine blast on Cambodia: Thailand military

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a strong denial on Friday against Thai allegations that Preah Vihear Temple is being used as a military base. The spokesperson stated that the temple is a sacred cultural site and has never been used for military purposes. The ministry highlighted that the site and surrounding areas under Cambodian sovereignty have suffered significant damage from past Thai military attacks and airstrikes. They emphasized that the presence of security guards is strictly for heritage protection and does not constitute a military presence.
title: Cambodian Foreign Ministry Reacts: Preah Vihear Temple is Not a Military Base

summary: Government Spokesperson Pen Bona reported that PM Hun Manet returned from international missions on Feb 26, having sought global support for Cambodia's territorial integrity. Domestically, the government facilitated a visit by the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) to Preah Vihear and An Seh on Feb 26 to inspect civilian areas damaged by Thai military attacks in late 2025. The government reiterated its position that Thai forces are 'illegally occupying' Cambodian land and using barbed wire to block displaced residents from returning home.
title: Cambodia Highlights Active Diplomacy on Border Situation with Thailand

summary: Acting Foreign Minister Eat Sophea led foreign diplomats and UN agencies to Banteay Meanchey to inspect Chouk Chey, Prey Chan, and Boeung Trakuon—areas reportedly occupied by Thai forces. The visit highlighted that residents are still barred from returning by Thai shipping containers and barbed wire, while civilian structures have been demolished. Nearly 10,000 displaced people are currently living in makeshift shelters at local pagodas.
title: Diplomatic Corps Inspects Disputed Border Sites as Displacement Crisis Persists

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet emphasized Cambodia's desire for de-escalation while defending the country's territorial integrity. He stated that Cambodia is seeking peaceful resolutions and has sought historical documentation from France to support its claims. The Prime Minister noted that the December ceasefire remains fragile, with Cambodian authorities alleging that Thai forces are still occupying certain areas.
title: Hun Manet bats for calm amid border dispute with Thailand

summary: Tensions are expected to rise as the Thai administration prepares to scrap MOU 44, the 2001 agreement regarding overlapping maritime claims in the Gulf of Thailand. The move comes as Cambodia continues a 'three-front campaign' involving border pressure, international diplomacy, and information warfare. The Royal Thai Army has also warned it will strike deep into Cambodian territory if PHL-03 rocket launchers are used against Thailand.
title: Thai-Cambodia standoff risks flare-up with MOU 44 set for scrapping

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Culture and Fine Arts issued a formal statement rejecting allegations that the UNESCO-listed Preah Vihear Temple has been used as a military base. The ministry emphasized its commitment to the 1954 Hague Convention, stating any security presence is strictly for protection.
title: Cambodia denies using Temple of Preah Vihear as military base in conflict

summary: Reports from the Joint Information Center and military social media groups indicate that Cambodia is moving at least 4-5 companies of newly trained soldiers and artillery units to the 'front line' as of Feb 28. This mobilization follows a period of clashes in late 2025. Thai authorities are monitoring the situation closely and reinforcing their own defensive positions as Cambodia reportedly fills gaps left by previous casualties.
title: Eyes on the Border! Cambodia Drafts New Troops, Massive Deployment Spotted Near Frontier

summary: Thai military officials report that Cambodian forces have been covertly planting landmines in areas claimed as Thai territory. The Army warned units to exercise extreme caution, noting that more mines may be discovered in disputed border zones.
title: Army reveals Cambodia smuggling landmines, more locations expected

summary: The 45th annual Cobra Gold exercise commenced at U-Tapao with 30 nations participating. Meanwhile, Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow addressed the UN Human Rights Council to clarify the border situation, claiming Cambodia is attempting to paint Thailand as the aggressor on the international stage while Thailand remains committed to a sustainable ceasefire.
title: Cobra Gold 2026 starts as FM Sihasak defends Thailand at UNHRC

summary: Tensions are expected to rise as reports emerge that the incoming Thai administration may scrap MOU 44, a 2001 agreement on offshore energy resources. Analysts suggest Cambodia is likely to maintain pressure across 'three fronts': the border, international diplomatic channels, and information space. The Thai Army has reportedly warned of retaliation if advanced weaponry like PHL-03 rocket systems are used by Cambodia.
title: Thai-Cambodia standoff risks flare-up with MOU 44 set for scrapping

summary: Lt. Gen. Weerayut Raksilp, Commander of the 2nd Army Region, visited the Suranaree Force at the Thai-Cambodian border to oversee security. He ordered troops to raise safety measures to the highest level, focusing on combat readiness and intelligence gathering to reassure local residents amidst ongoing watch status.
title: Army Region 2 Commander visits border to upgrade security and intelligence

summary: The Thai Foreign Ministry updated ASEAN on the border situation, confirming that Thailand is strictly following the ceasefire. Additionally, the military has resumed limited fuel exports to Laos but with strict GPS tracking to prevent the fuel from being diverted to Cambodia.
title: Govt tells ASEAN it is pressing ahead with regional peace efforts
